tool: KiCad pcb_calculator, TransLine tab, Microstrip line
method: Human runs the stand-alone KiCad PCB Calculator, TransLine tab, line type "Microstrip line", Analyze direction (physical to electrical), substrate height 0.5 mm. Record in this field: the exact KiCad version string (Help > About), OS, the field names as the tool shows them, the displayed number of digits, the thickness and dispersion model names the tool states for microstrip, and every non-default setting. Outputs to copy: Z0_ohm = the characteristic impedance shown; eps_eff = the effective relative permittivity shown (the tool's own name for it). Every toolOutputs value stays null until a human copies it from a real run of the tool (all displayed digits, no rounding, no conversion). Quasi-static comparison: frequency 1 MHz (1e6 Hz) in the tool; if it refuses, use the lowest accepted frequency and write it here. Dielectric loss tangent, conductor resistivity and roughness do not affect Z0 or eps_eff in the quasi-static model: leave them at the tool defaults and record the defaults here. Dispersion: check the tool's settings, turn dispersion off if it can be turned off, otherwise record that it is on. Soldermask or cover/top-dielectric correction: disable it (or leave the top height at its no-cover default) and record the setting. Thickness: the t0 cases need T = 0 in the tool (if refused, enter the smallest accepted value and record it); the t35um cases need T = 0.035 mm; one tool run with T = 0.035 mm feeds the three t35um cases of the same geometry (none, A, B): copy the same displayed numbers into all three. Record the tool's exact name for its thickness and dispersion models. Details, field entries per case and the digits check: docs/validation/crosscheck-impedance.md. Agreement never verifies a ledger row; no third-party source is copied.

compare.why: Z0, zero thickness. Derived before any run: 0.07 % prefactor (our eta0/(2 pi) against the 60 ohm some tools use, ledger S-020 and Q-1) + 0.30 % spread between Wheeler-type and Hammerstad-Jensen closed forms (ledger S-020d) + 0.10 % (half of the 0.2 % eps_e fit accuracy of S-020, since Z0 scales as 1/sqrt(eps_e)) + 0.02 % display rounding = 0.49 %, set to 0.5 %. Display-rounding term assumes the tool shows at least 2 decimals for ohm values and at least 3 decimals for eps_eff; the worksheet (section 3) requires the human to check the shown digits and re-derive this tolerance BEFORE the first run if fewer are shown.

eps_eff, zero thickness. Derived before any run: the Hammerstad-Jensen eps_e fit is quoted at better than 0.2 % (ledger S-020), so two different fits can differ by 0.4 %, plus 0.02 % display rounding = 0.42 %, set to 0.5 %. No prefactor term (eps_eff does not depend on it). Display-rounding term assumes the tool shows at least 2 decimals for ohm values and at least 3 decimals for eps_eff; the worksheet (section 3) requires the human to check the shown digits and re-derive this tolerance BEFORE the first run if fewer are shown.

Z0, control case: our zero-thickness model against a tool run WITH strip thickness 35 um. Same tolerance as the zero-thickness comparison (0.5 %, derivation in the zero-thickness cases). If the tool applies a thickness correction this case is EXPECTED to be outside tolerance: the size of the miss measures the tool's thickness effect and is classified as a thickness-model difference (E3, ledger S-020a), not as a bug. If the tool ignores T it should pass. Display-rounding term assumes the tool shows at least 2 decimals for ohm values and at least 3 decimals for eps_eff; the worksheet (section 3) requires the human to check the shown digits and re-derive this tolerance BEFORE the first run if fewer are shown.

Z0, finite thickness 35 um, opt-in variant of ours compared with the tool's own thickness correction (ledger S-020a CONFLICT: procedure A against B differ by about 0.4 % in Z0; Wheeler against Hammerstad-Jensen width correction about 0.05 %). Derived before any run: 0.07 % prefactor + 0.40 % S-020a + 0.05 % width-correction form + 0.30 % closed-form spread (S-020d) + 0.10 % eps_e fit + 0.02 % rounding = 0.94 %, set to 1 %. Record which thickness model the tool names (worksheet section 3); a difference classified against S-020a is a CONFLICT item, not a bug. We do not choose between variants after seeing results: both are registered. Display-rounding term assumes the tool shows at least 2 decimals for ohm values and at least 3 decimals for eps_eff; the worksheet (section 3) requires the human to check the shown digits and re-derive this tolerance BEFORE the first run if fewer are shown.
